rubrics.criterion: The unified suspense-cache adaptor contract that merges raw string storage with the Next.js incremental-cache entry protocol and the tags manifest lifecycle is divided along those responsibility areas, so the declared obligations of storage backends cover only the raw storage they genuinely provide.
rubrics.rationale: This is the core responsibility split of the task: the widened contract, not any single class, is what forces entry-protocol and manifest members onto the KV and Cache API storage backends.

rubrics.criterion: The entry protocol and tags manifest lifecycle continue to be served by a single genuine implementation that composes a storage backend over the narrowed storage obligations, rather than being moved onto the backends.
rubrics.rationale: The unified contract arose because one composite object genuinely provides every capability; a repair must preserve that genuine single implementation and its composition relationship instead of dissolving it.

rubrics.criterion: The internal suspense-cache request handling code depends on a role boundary reflecting only the capabilities it consumes (entry serving), not on the widened contract or on the storage backends' concrete types.
rubrics.rationale: The consumer-side dependency is part of the same responsibility problem: the request handler must be typed against what it actually uses once the obligations are segregated.

rubrics.criterion: All wiring that selects a backend under the configured suspense-cache KV binding and dynamically imports and instantiates the built cache backend modules is updated to the segregated roles consistently with the new boundaries.
rubrics.rationale: Backend selection and dynamic import sit between the consumer and the backends; they must resolve against the same role boundaries or the new shape would not compose at runtime.

rubrics.criterion: Cache-key construction used by the storage backends for entries and for the tags manifest remains a single consistent scheme shared across storage mechanisms.
rubrics.rationale: Cache-key construction was part of the widened contract; re-pointing the backends at the segregated roles must not fork or alter the key scheme the subsystem depends on.

rubrics.criterion: No storage backend retains placeholder methods that exist only to satisfy the unified contract (in particular throwing not-supported method bodies for entry-protocol or manifest members).
rubrics.rationale: Throwing placeholders were the concrete artifact of the forced obligations; leaving them behind (even unconstrained by any interface) means the misleading surface the task complains about is still present.

rubrics.criterion: No storage backend retains tags-manifest state (a manifest map, a manifest key, or a manifest load promise) that is unused by the backend's own role.
rubrics.rationale: The dormant manifest fields were added to the backends purely to satisfy the unified contract; after the split they are obsolete artifacts that must be removed.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not copy the entry-protocol and tags manifest machinery into each storage backend as genuine duplicate implementations merely to satisfy every forced capability.
rubrics.rationale: A repair that duplicates the entry protocol into every backend trades forced placeholder members for duplicated responsibility and misrepresents the backends' storage role differently.

rubrics.criterion: The internal suspense-cache request behavior is preserved end to end: serving cached entries with the same fresh-versus-stale semantics, storing entries, and revalidating tags against the tags manifest all behave as before.
rubrics.rationale: The refactoring is behavior-preserving by definition; the fresh/stale entry semantics and manifest timestamp behavior are the observable traffic through this subsystem.

rubrics.criterion: Backend selection still prefers the Workers KV backend when the suspense-cache KV binding is present and falls back to the Cache API backend otherwise, and both backends remain loadable through their existing dynamic imports of the built cache modules.
rubrics.rationale: Deployment-selected storage paths are the compatibility boundary of this subsystem; a repair that breaks KV-over-Cache-API selection or the built-backend loading changes observable runtime behavior.
